chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:

I asked him about a man who sells to a group collectively: he carries for this one one load, for this one two loads, and for this one three loads, and some of the goods are superior. Then a bit. So a man comes to him and says, 'Sell them all to me.' He said, 'It does not please me.'

key_terms.فَيَأْتِيهِ الرَّجُلُ: then the man comes to him
key_terms.يَحْمِلُ إِلَيْهِ الْحَمَلَةُ: he carries for him a load

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling goods collectively when quantities and qualities vary?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses disapproval of selling mixed goods collectively when their individual qualities and quantities vary, as this introduces *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the specific portion the buyer receives. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision in commercial transactions to prevent disputes, contrasting with more lenient views on collective sales (*bay' al-kala'*) when the goods are uniform or clearly defined.
